title: e2e throughput trace playbook
content:
TL;DR: Continuous-batcher misconfiguration + skewed prompt-length distribution caused a ~60% tokens/sec regression on host xg-alloc-7 between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-03. This is my scratchpad playbook for repro, quick mitigations, and long-term fixes.

Context / how I found it:
- Alert: per-model tokens/sec dropped from median ~32k -> 12k; p95 latency rose from 120ms -> 420ms.
- Affected model: rwinf/gptx-16k-v2 (quantized variant), route: /v1/generate (hosted pool: hosted-eu-4).
- First noticed by pager (SRE) when downstream customer churn alarm fired (CS ticket CS-657).

Hypothesis summary (first pass):
1) Continuous batching (cbatch) was using conservative max_delay (CBATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=12) plus an aggressive small-batch flush policy. With heavy variance in prompt lengths (short prompts spiking), batches ended up tiny and kernel switching happened more often -> GPU occupancy dropped.
2) A config rollout (autodeploy: serving-runtime 3.7.1) accidentally reverted a tuned cbatch heuristic (redwood.io/batcher-prefs) to defaults.
3) KV-prefetch/cache hit-rate dropped (cache_miss increased) because prefixes changed with new personalization tokens, increasing average sequence length per request and causing more OOM/alloc churn.

What I ran (raw commands + notes)
- tail the host logs and grep batcher flush reasons:
  kubectl -n serving logs pod/hosted-eu-4-xg-alloc-7 -c runtime | grep -E "batcher:|kvcache|kernel_select" -n | tail -200
  # sample output snippets I captured:
  # [2025-11-02T18:32:14Z] batcher: flush triggered (max_delay_ms reached=12, batch_size=3)
  # [2025-11-02T18:32:14Z] batcher: small-batch flush (variance high, expected_more=false)
  # [2025-11-02T18:32:14Z] kernel_select: chosen=fp16-default, fallback=int8-emu (time_ms=78)

- Confirmed model variant switchover frequency (grep count of kernel_select):
  kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/hosted-eu-4-xg-alloc-7 -- sh -c "grep -c \"kernel_select\" /var/log/runtime.log"
  # result: 1432 kernel_select events in 1h (suspicious high).

- Check GPU utilization and queue depth (nvidia-smi + runtime metrics):
  kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/hosted-eu-4-xg-alloc-7 -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv -l 5s -f 12s
  # observed: util avg ~22% (was ~78% before regression).

- Run a synthetic load driver to reproduce (python snippet I used):
  # save as tools/load_driver/vary_len_driver.py (quick local run)
  import time, requests, random
  URL = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
  headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer $TEST_KEY", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
  def make_prompt(l):
      return "Q:" + "x"*l
  def call(l):
      data = {"model": "rwinf/gptx-16k-v2", "input": make_prompt(l), "max_tokens": 64}
      r = requests.post(URL, json=data, headers=headers, timeout=10)
      return r.status_code, len(r.content)
  # run 200 concurrent small-only (l=10) vs mixed (l random between 10 and 2500) epochs

- Observed repro: mixed-length traffic reduces tokens/sec drastically; short-only traffic keeps throughput high. Means variance in sequence lengths is a key factor.

Quick mitigations tried (notes + results)
- 2025-11-03 03:20 - revert cbatch heuristic to tuned values (redwood.io/batcher-pref: max_delay_ms=28, min_batch_tokens=256, variance_threshold=0.32) via k8s ConfigMap patch -> immediate tokens/sec recovered to ~26k but p95 still elevated. (rollback PR: github.com/.../pull/998)
- 2025-11-03 03:45 - temporarily force single kernel path by setting env FORCE_KERNEL=fp16-default on pool -> latency improved but CPU thread contention observed. Not a long-term fix.
- 2025-11-03 04:10 - increase cbatch concurrency (redwood.io/batcher-concurrency=6) -> improved throughput marginally, but more context switches.

Error snippets / notable logs I collected
- runtime stderr:
  E1123 18:32:14.564 kernel_selector.cc:124] kernel: fallback to int8-emu due to insufficient workspace (need 1.2GB, avail 0.9GB)
  W1123 18:32:14.565 batcher.cc:341] batcher: flush_small_batch (size=3) triggered by variance
  I1123 18:32:14.566 kv_cache.cc:88] kvcache: miss (prefix_id=abcd1234)

- grpc perf counters (from /metrics):
  redwood_rpc_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="generate",le="0.1"} 0
  redwood_rpc_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="generate",le="0.5"} 0
  redwood_rpc_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="generate",le="1.0"} 12
  # shows a huge shift toward higher buckets vs baseline.

Repro steps (fast path for SRE to reproduce in staging)
1) Deploy serving-runtime:3.7.1 on staging pool (staging-eu-2) and enable default cbatch config used in prod at time-of-incident (I attached the config to INFRA-2127).
2) Use load driver: tools/load_driver/vary_len_driver.py with two profiles:
   - profile A: 200 concurrent clients, len=16 constant (baseline)
   - profile B: 200 concurrent clients, len randomly uniform(8, 2200) (regression pattern)
3) Monitor /metrics for tokens/sec and kernel_select count, nvidia util, and batcher flush reasons.

Diagnostic checks to run quickly (ordered)
- cbatch config: kubectl get cm serving-runtime-batcher -n serving -o yaml | egrep -A3 "max_delay|min_batch_tokens|variance"
- kernel fallback rate: grep -c "fallback to int8-emu" /var/log/runtime.log (high count -> memory fragmentation/alloc issues)
- kvcache hit ratio: redis-cli HGET stats kvcache_hit_rate (or check metrics: redwood_kvcache_hit_ratio)
- per-route sequence length distribution: curl -s http://localhost:9102/metrics | grep seq_length_bucket | sort -n | tail -20

Notes / theory on root cause (what I'd bet on)
- The main amplifier is variance in seq lengths coupled with too-small max_delay_ms -> batches flush prematurely instead of waiting for a few more inbound requests that would make a dense batch. That yields many small batches with low token density, failing to amortize kernel launch overhead.
- Secondary factor: a subtle mem-fragmentation/regression in the allocator after a model-config change caused workspace shortages and kernel fallback to slower int8 emulation path.

Longer-term fixes and experiments to prioritize
- Make cbatch more workload-aware: adaptive max_delay_ms based on recent seq_length variance (EWMA).
- Add a fast path for short-running requests: pack short prompts into a separate micro-batcher tuned for small tokens (min_batch_tokens lower but grouped).
- Improve kernel selection hysteresis so we don't flip kernels for small differences in required workspace. Add per-worker sticky-kernel preference for N minutes.
- Add more telemetry: batch_token_density and kernel_switch_count per minute per-pool.

Open TODOs (me / handoff)
- [ ] Finish a minimal reproducer harness with deterministic seeds (tools/load_driver/recipe_mixed.yaml) — Samir (ETA 2025-11-09)
- [ ] Push a safer cbatch config rollout (staged canary) and create alert for kernel_switch_rate spiking — Lina (linked PR draft in GH).
- [ ] Attach heap snapshots from the allocator with debug builds when we can reproduce OOM/fallback — Asha.
- [ ] Add doc page (confluence) summarizing playbook and knobs (owner: Samir).

Random notes to self:
- Watch for AUTOSCALER annotations that touch pod CPU limits; small CPU budget -> worker thread starvation -> fewer batching decisions processed.
- Check the release notes for serving-runtime 3.7.1 (there's a line about "allocator tweaks" that I think corresponds to this).
- Consider a small config: set CBATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS to 40ms for 48h and monitor — quick A/B.

Breadcrumbs: short timeline
- 2025-10-30: steady-state, tokens/sec baseline ~32k.
- 2025-10-31 22:14: new runtime rollout 3.7.1 (canary).
- 2025-11-01: small increase in kernel_switch_count observed in canary pool.
- 2025-11-02 17:58: full rollout. Regression becomes systemic between 11/02-11/03.
- 2025-11-03 03:20: emergency rollback/patch of cbatch heuristics recovered most of throughput.

If you pick this up (hand-off checklist):
- Run the reproducible harness in staging, attach metrics dashboard (I used grafana dash id: dash-serve-34)
- Don't change quantization variants mid-investigation (makes tracing harder). Pin model: rwinf/gptx-16k-v2@v12.
- When returning to prod configs, do a canary on 5% of pool for 2h, watch kernel_switch_count and tokens/sec.

End of scratchpad. This doc is messy on purpose — use it as a breadcrumb trail; I kept raw grep outputs and commands so someone on-call can copy/paste. If we converge on a blameless root cause we can extract a polished postmortem.

-- Samir
